text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server often responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. However, you must handle authentication, often through an API key or token, to prove you have permission to access the data. You should also respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, always include error handling, because network problems or invalid requests can happen at any time.
